scope: SimpleLink wireless families: CC13x0/CC26x0, CC13x2/CC26x2, CC13x2x7/CC26x2x7, CC13x1/CC26x1, CC13x4/CC26x4, CC23xx, CC27xx, CC32xx, CC33xx, CC35xx. Research only; no board was touched. Sources: CCStudio 21.0.1 targetdb and GEL, UniFlash 9.6.0 (DSLite, propertyDB, target_setup.json), xPack OpenOCD 0.12.0-7 scripts, TI's OpenOCD fork scripts and driver source (ti-release cb22a31e), SimpleLink Low Power F3 SDK 9.21.00.36, F2 SDK 8.33.00.16 (archived copy), Wi-Fi Toolbox 4.3.23, TI datasheets SWRS181D, SWRS204C, SWRS207J, SWRS215E, SWRS253B, SWRS258B, SWRS267B, SWRS268B, SWRS272F, SWRS294F, SWRS304D, SWRS306E, SWRS337B and TRMs SWCU117I, SWCU185G, SWCU192, SWCU193A, SWCU194, SWCU195A. Repo measured facts are cited by path. 'unknown' means no file read answers it.

probe_sequence.do: Read what the probe is (XDS110 on a LaunchPad, external LP-XDS110, CMSIS-DAP on others). Do not pick a tool by the user's word.

Try JTAG (with the cJTAG-to-4-pin escape sequence on XDS110) and read the ICEPick IDCODE (IR 0x04). Mask 0x0FFFFFFF. A hit in {0x0B99A02F, 0x0B9BE02F, 0x0BB4102F, 0x0BB7702F, 0x0BB7A02F, 0x0BB7802F} identifies the CC13xx/CC26xx subfamily. These chips do not answer SWD.

If JTAG is silent, wake SWD from dormant (selection alert, activation 0x1A, line reset) and read DPIDR. 0x2BA01477 (TI's cfg expectation for CC23xx) or 0x6BA02477 (measured on a CC2755P10) means CC23xx or CC27xx; 0x4BA02477 with AP0 0x102E0001 means CC35xx. Then read CFG-AP DEVICEID and apply the mask.
CC32xx: the SOP straps pick SWD (Fn2WJ) or 4-pin JTAG (Fn4WJ); try both, then expect DAP 0x2BA01477 (SWD) or 0x4BA00477 behind ICEPick 0x0B97C02F (JTAG).
Identify the member: CC13x4 USER_ID at 0x50000A94 (CC13 bit 23, PA bit 25, PKG 18:16); M3/M4 parts USER_ID at 0x50001294; CC23/CC27 PARTID variant byte (bits 23:16) through CFG-AP reg 0x04.
probe_sequence.source: SWCU194 Table 11-60; TI fork cc26xx.h; cc23xx.c, cc27xx.c

probe_sequence.do: Writes: CC13xx/CC26xx use DSLite with the sector-level erase default and a main-flash-only image; no tool in the files writes CC23xx or CC27xx main flash without a chip erase except our community OpenOCD driver; CC35xx uses the Toolbox.

write_paths.detail: ROM serial bootloader over UART0 or SPI0, same packet protocol on both. recovery.symptom: Debugger connects only in the first seconds after power-on, then Error -242 (measured on the CC1354P10)
recovery.fix: Power-cycle the probe's USB port and connect at once; or xds110reset. A running program that sleeps or reconfigures the debug pins closes the window.

recovery.symptom: CPU DAP or TAP locked by the CCFG

Commands: PING 0x20, DOWNLOAD 0x21, GET_STATUS 0x23, SEND_DATA 0x24, RESET 0x25, SECTOR_ERASE 0x26, CRC32 0x27, GET_CHIP_ID 0x28, MEMORY_READ 0x2A, MEMORY_WRITE 0x2B, BANK_ERASE 0x2C, SET_CCFG 0x2D, DOWNLOAD_CRC 0x2F. write_paths.detail: UniFlash 9.6.0 DSLite `flash` with a ccxml. CC2340R2/R5 property file (CC23xx_FlashProperties.xml) offers only FlashEraseSetting = 'Chip Erase' (default), 'Chip Erase (retain sectors specified in CCFG)' or 'Do not erase sectors (program load only)'. There is no per-sector erase choice, so a program load with any erase is a chip erase. CC2341 uses CC23x1_FlashProperties.xml with NoFlashErase, RetainMainSectors and RetainCcfgScfg instead. Skip-sectors (FlashPageToggle/FlashPages, e.g. '0-5,8') excludes sectors from erase, program and verify; whether it can name the CCFG sector was not shown in the files. Answer for the project: no documented DSLite option erases only the needed sectors on CC23xx. The no-erase choice programs only blank flash. Not run.

write_paths.detail: UniFlash 9.6.0 DSLite `flash`. CC27xx_FlashProperties.xml settings: NoFlashErase (default 0, 'Do not erase before program load'), RetainMainSectors (default 1, 'Retain MAIN sectors specified in existing CCFG', e.g. the HSM area), RetainCcfgScfg (default 0, 'Retain CCFG and SCFG sectors'). Default flash is a chip erase that clears CCFG and SCFG too (measured on the LP-EM-CC2755P10: docs/remote-board-recovery.md). Closest documented option to what the project needs: `-s RetainCcfgScfg=1` (with RetainMainSectors=1) and an image that holds main flash only, no CCFG or SCFG section. The files do not say which SACI erase (ERASE_MAIN_APP or ERASE_CHIP) DSLite sends for it, and it still erases all non-retained main sectors, not only the needed ones. `-s NoFlashErase=1` programs without erasing, valid only on blank sectors. Setting id spellings were not run. Not run.

debug_port.protocol: SWD | JTAG chosen by the sense-on-power (SOP) pins
debug_port.access: The SOP[2:0] pull levels at power-up pick the pin mapping: Fn2WJ (SOP 001, 2-pin SWD on TMS/TCK), Fn4WJ (SOP 000, 4-pin JTAG), LDfrUART_Fn4WJ (SOP 010) and UARTLOAD (SOP 100: waits for UART load, JTAG 4-wire). In JTAG a ICEPick-C router fronts the DAP; in SWD the DAP answers directly. OpenOCD cfg: SWD DAP ID 0x2BA01477, JTAG DAP 0x4BA00477, ICEPick JRC TAP ID 0x0B97C02F (version ignored). UniFlash has separate '_SWD' device entries for the 2-pin case.
debug_port.notes: On our parked CC3200-LAUNCHXL the JTAG chain read all ones and SWD said 'cannot read IDR' with SOP jumpers as received and removed.
